overview: Malawi's women's health innovation landscape is driven less by venture-backed femtech startups and more by government mHealth programs, donor-funded maternal and newborn health initiatives, drone logistics, and a dense network of menstrual-health social enterprises and NGOs. National priorities center on cutting maternal mortality (a headline target of 110 per 100,000 by 2030), expanding contraception, and ending period poverty. Digital tools like the government-adopted Chipatala Cha Pa Foni hotline and community health worker apps such as YendaNafe extend care into rural areas, while drone corridors move blood and samples to remote facilities. The homegrown femtech startup layer remains thin, with most momentum coming from public health systems and civil society.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent activity clusters around maternal health financing, menstrual equity advocacy, and drone scale-up.

items.text: World Menstrual Hygiene Day in Malawi led by the Ministry of Health and Sanitation, focused on ending stigma and building a period-friendly environment.
The Beginnings Fund launched to deploy up to USD 500 million over five years for maternal and newborn health across 10 African countries including Malawi.
Malawi finalizes a Collaborative Advocacy Action Plan setting five advocacy goals to strengthen women's, children's and adolescents' health accountability.
Coverage highlights how drones are bridging healthcare access gaps in Malawi, including maternal health supply delivery to remote areas.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Policy is anchored on maternal mortality reduction, reproductive rights legislation, and menstrual product affordability.

items.text: Government commits to raise the reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health share of the national health budget to 30% by 2030 and finalize a comprehensive SRHR legal framework.
Malawi government removes duty and excise tax on sanitary pads, a menstrual-equity policy win advocated for by AHF Africa and local coalitions.
Malawi commits at the Nairobi ICPD Summit to lower maternal mortality to 110 per 100,000 live births by 2030.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Momentum is concentrated in government mHealth, community health worker tools, and drone logistics rather than private startups.

items.text: Chipatala Cha Pa Foni (Health Center by Phone), a maternal and child health hotline and SMS service, was adopted by the government and remains in active use, with 2025 research examining rural uptake.
YendaNafe, an Android mHealth app, deployed to community health workers in rural Neno district to improve maternal health coverage.
Integrated Community Health Information System (iCHIS) rolled out by the Ministry of Health to digitize patient records and monitor maternal and child health at community level.
VillageReach and partners scaling national drone corridors to move blood, lab samples, vaccines and medicines to remote maternal health facilities.
Ripple Africa ran 2024-2025 pilot phases distributing 2,750 menstrual cups to schoolgirls, teachers and women, reporting improved school attendance.

sections.heading: Key players & hubs
sections.narrative: The active players span government mHealth, NGO menstrual-health enterprises, drone logistics and Malawi's original tech hub.

items.name: VillageReach
items.note: Leads drone-for-health logistics with the Ministry of Health, moving blood and samples to remote maternal facilities since 2016

items.name: Days for Girls Malawi
items.note: National menstrual-health program active since 2014; distributed ~46,000 washable pad kits and drove tax-removal advocacy

items.name: UNFPA Malawi
items.note: Runs nationwide period-friendly campaign and supports maternal health and family planning programming

items.name: mHub
items.note: Malawi's first tech and innovation hub (Lilongwe and Blantyre), founded by Rachel Sibande; incubates tech ventures and trains young women in digital skills

items.name: Supreme (social enterprise)
items.note: Malawi-based social enterprise making reusable sanitary pads and diapers, reinvesting profits into menstrual education

items.name: Grace Pads
items.note: Lilongwe-based charity combining sanitation, education and business to empower young Malawian women through menstrual products

items.name: The Sparkle Foundation
items.note: Runs menstrual health management plus financial-literacy and IT training for teenage girls in rural Malawi

items.name: Ripple Africa
items.note: Piloted menstrual cup distribution (2,750 cups) to schoolgirls and women in 2024-2025

items.name: Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI)
items.note: Supports Malawi Ministry of Health on digital health systems, supply chain and access to essential services

items.name: Chikondi Girls Project Malawi
items.note: Founded by Enelless Pemba; advocates reusable sanitary pads to help girls manage periods with dignity
